explain.say: A cooling tower gets rid of a power station's waste heat. Warm water from the condenser, at around 35 to 40 degrees Celsius, is pumped up into the bottom of the tower.

faq.q: Is the white plume from a cooling tower smoke?
faq.a: No, it is clean water vapour that condenses into tiny droplets as it meets cooler air, just like your breath on a cold day. Smoke from burning fuel leaves through a separate, thinner chimney.
asks: What comes out of a cooling tower?

faq.q: Why are cooling towers shaped like that?
faq.a: The curved shape, called a hyperboloid, is very strong for the small amount of concrete it uses and can be built from straight beams. Its height helps the warm air rise strongly and pull cool air in at the base.
asks: Why do cooling towers have a curved shape?

faq.q: Where does the hot water come from?
faq.a: It comes from the condenser, where it has cooled the used steam from the turbine. The cooling water and the boiler water run in separate pipes and never mix.
asks: Is the cooling water the same as the steam?

faq.q: Are cooling towers only for nuclear power?
faq.a: No. Coal and gas stations have them too, because every steam power station must dump waste heat. Stations beside the sea or a big river often skip towers and use that water directly.
asks: Do nuclear stations have cooling towers?

faq.q: How much water does a cooling tower use?
faq.a: A tower evaporates roughly 1 to 2 percent of the water flowing through it, which can be hundreds of litres every second at a big station. That water has to be topped up from a river or lake.

facts: The curved shape of a classic cooling tower is called a hyperboloid.
Evaporating one kilogram of water takes over 2 million joules of heat, which is why evaporation cools so well.

quiz.say: What mainly carries the heat away in a cooling tower?
quiz.show: In a cooling tower, the heat leaves by…
quiz.why: Evaporating a little of the water takes a lot of heat from the rest, and the warm moist air carries it up and away.

wrong.1: No fuel burns in a cooling tower; the plume is water.
wrong.2: No ice is used; evaporation does the cooling.
